newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes down at 1,300-1,450 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes down at 1,300-1,450 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 1,300-1,450 per dollar, down from the morning's 1,200-1,300 and sharply lower than 1,020-1,040 at Tuesday's close, amid extremely jittery interbank forex trade, dealers said.
"Trade was extremely hectic. The lev lost some 40 percent from Tuesday as dollar demand ran high amid very low supply," one dealer said.
Traded volumes were small because banks remained reluctant to sell amid ongoing political instability.
"The recent sharp lev depreciation and expectations of rising political and social tensions made banks very cautious," the dealer said.
The lev opened at 930/950 on Monday and traded near 600 at the beginning of the year.
The ruling Socialist party has decided to insist on forming a new government despite opposition protests, now in their 24th day, and a presidential appeal to agree to early general elections.

In a bid to alleviate pressure on the lev, the central bank decided on Wednesday to temporarily ban commercial banks from using their minimum required reserves for emergency refinancing, effective Thursday.
"This will probably give the lev a short-term break but more certainly, it would disturb interbank settlement payments," a trader said.
So far, local commercial banks have been allowed to use daily up to 30 percent of their minimum required reserves at the central bank for emergency refinancing.

Meanwhile, Bulgarian debt suffered a blow after Bulgarian president Petar Stoyanov told NATO ambassadors during a visit to Brussels that Bulgaria could default on its debt repayments unless it received financial help for its collapsing economy. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
